question: As per the 10th consecutive Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, what is the repo rate at which the Reserve Bank of India lends to banks as on 30th October 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**3) 0.065**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• As of October 30, 2024, the repo rate at which the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) lends to banks is **0.065**.
 
• The repo rate is a critical tool used by the RBI to control inflation and regulate the money supply in the economy.
 
• This rate is determined by the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) which meets bi-monthly to review and set the repo rate.
 
• The repo rate influences the interest rates offered by banks on loans and deposits, affecting borrowing and spending in the economy.
 
• A lower repo rate typically aims to encourage borrowing and investment, stimulating economic growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)**

 
 
• The MPC is a committee of the RBI responsible for formulating the monetary policy of India.
 
• It consists of six members: three officials from the RBI and three external members appointed by the Government of India.
 
• The primary objective of the MPC is to maintain price stability while keeping in mind the objective of economic growth.
 
 
 
• **Repo Rate**
 
 
• The repo rate is the rate at which the central bank of a country (RBI in India) lends money to commercial banks in the event of any shortfall of funds.
 
• It is used by monetary authorities to control inflation.
 
• A decrease in the repo rate can lead to banks reducing their lending rates, making loans cheaper and boosting consumption and investment.
 
 
 
• **Reverse Repo Rate**
 
 
• The reverse repo rate is the rate at which the RBI borrows money from commercial banks.
 
• It is used to control the money supply in the economy.
 
• A higher reverse repo rate encourages banks to park more funds with the RBI, thereby reducing the money supply in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Inflation Control**
 
 
• The RBI uses various monetary policy tools, including the repo rate, to control inflation.
 
• High inflation can erode purchasing power and hurt economic growth, while very low inflation can lead to deflation, where prices fall continuously.
 
• Maintaining a balance is crucial for a stable economic environment.
